org: Museu de Ciencies Naturals de Barcelona (Jardi Botanic + Jardi Botanic Historic)
why_them: Four of our Barcelona trees stand in their Jardi Botanic Historic at the Sot de l'Estany (the wingnut bcn_005, green ash bcn_006, ash bcn_021, sycamore bcn_022) and two of the four have no photograph.

org: Institut Botanic de Barcelona (IBB, CSIC-CMCNB)
why_them: The research institute sitting inside the Jardi Botanic on Montjuic, next to the Sot de l'Estany hollow where our oldest Barcelona survivors (bcn_005, bcn_006) grow; the obvious people to check our species identifications.

org: Reggia di Caserta
why_them: All seven Caserta trees we publish stand in their Giardino Inglese, including the Cedar of the Palco and the Yew of the Bath of Venus, and every single one of the seven is missing a photograph.

org: Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte
why_them: Eight of Naples' seventeen trees are theirs, in the Giardino dei Principi and the Real Fruttiera (the camphors, the Montezuma cypress, the Cretan palm that survived the war), and all eight lack a photograph.

org: Orto Botanico di Roma (Sapienza Universita di Roma)
why_them: Two of our Rome entries are theirs: the Twin Planes of the Eleven Fountains (rom_003) and the Cork Oak of the Orangery (rom_004), and the cork oak still has no photograph.

org: RAMI - Il Registro degli Alberi Monumentali d'Italia
why_them: We cite their field records as a source on a dozen Rome trees, including the Magnolia of Via Corsini and the Holm Oak of Piazza Perin del Vaga, where their access note settled whether the tree could be visited at all.

org: Istituto Italiano di Studi Germanici (Villa Sciarra)
why_them: The institute occupies the villa in the middle of Villa Sciarra, and rom_011 is literally the Himalayan Cedar of the German Institute standing in their own grounds; the Area acquisti e servizi generali is the office that looks after the building and garden.

org: Musei in Comune Roma (Sovrintendenza Capitolina, Villa Torlonia and Villa Borghese museums)
why_them: The Cedar of Lebanon of Villa Torlonia (rom_018) stands at the entrance staircase of their own Casino Nobile, and the Hackberries of the Aranciera (rom_022) grow beside the Museo Carlo Bilotti in Villa Borghese; both are unphotographed.

org: Patronato del Real Alcazar y de la Casa Consistorial de Sevilla
why_them: Two Seville entries are inside their walls: the Ginkgo Grove of the Jardin Ingles (sev_001) and the Pecan in the Jardin del Marques de la Vega Inclan (sev_014), and the pecan has no photograph.

org: Jardi Botanic de la Universitat de Valencia
why_them: Their Kashmir Cypress (vlc_010) and Caucasian Elm (vlc_015) are two of Valencia's sixteen trees and neither has a photograph on our page.

org: Real Jardin Botanico de Madrid (CSIC)
why_them: The Cypress of the Plano de la Flor terrace (mad_005) and the Caucasian Elm of the Paseo de Mutis (mad_006) are theirs, and their Unidad de Jardin y Arbolado is the team that measures exactly the trees we describe.

org: Park Guell (Barcelona Serveis Municipals)
why_them: Four of our Barcelona trees are inside their park: the Carob of the Viaduct (bcn_002), the Regrown Carob of the Placa de la Natura (bcn_003), the Wild Olive of the east sector (bcn_016) and the Mastic of Hort de l'Avi (bcn_033); three of them have no photograph.

org: Asociacion Espanola de Arboricultura
why_them: They are the people who prune and assess exactly the trees we map, and the Ombu of Placa Prim in Barcelona and the Ombu of La Cartuja in Seville are the kind of structurally odd veterans their members write about.

org: Asociacion Espanola de Parques y Jardines Publicos (AEPJP)
why_them: Their membership is the municipal parks departments of Madrid, Barcelona, Seville and Valencia, which is where most of our 100-plus Spanish trees stand, from the Retiro's ahuehuete to the Parque de Maria Luisa hackberries.

org: Bosques sin Fronteras
why_them: They run Spain's singular-tree work and would recognise El Titan, the giant ficus of Valencia's Parterre, and Seville's El Gran Capitan, both of which we publish and one of which we still cannot illustrate.

org: Societa Botanica Italiana (Gruppo Orti Botanici e Giardini Storici)
why_them: Their botanic-garden group covers the four Italian gardens we lean on hardest: the Orto Botanico di Roma, Brera in Milan, the Orto Botanico di Napoli and Florence's Giardino dei Semplici, where six of our fifteen Florence trees stand.

org: ISA Italia - Societa Italiana di Arboricoltura
why_them: Their arborists are the people who assess the veteran planes we publish in Milan's Giardini Montanelli, including Il Sacerdote and the 34-metre plane, neither of which we have a photograph of.

org: Italia Nostra
why_them: Their Rome section campaigns over the historic villas where half our Rome list stands, Villa Borghese, Villa Sciarra and Villa Doria Pamphilj, including the Cedar of the Belvedere above the Lago del Giglio.

org: Gallerie degli Uffizi (Giardino di Boboli)
why_them: The Cedar Above Pegasus (flo_008) stands in their Giardino del Cavaliere at the top of Boboli and is one of the Florence trees we still have no photograph of.

org: Orto Botanico Giardino dei Semplici, Sistema Museale UniFi
why_them: Six of our fifteen Florence trees are inside their walls, among them the Micheli Yew planted in 1720 and the Caucasian elm they cut back to save; the Himalayan Cedar of the Semplici (flo_014) is the one we cannot illustrate. Address published on their own page as edu(AT)sma.unifi.it.

org: Orto Botanico di Padova (Centro di Ateneo, Universita di Padova)
why_them: Four of Padua's nine trees are theirs, including Goethe's palm of 1585 and the 1786 magnolia (pad_004) which has no photograph; the address is their Settore promozione, gestione dei servizi al pubblico e comunicazione.

org: Basilica Pontificia di Sant'Antonio di Padova
why_them: The Magnolia of the Saint (pad_005) grows in their Chiostro della Magnolia, and the cloister is the one place in Padua where a visitor stands inside a monastery to look at the tree.

org: Orto Botanico di Brera (Universita degli Studi di Milano)
why_them: Their ginkgo (mil_004) is one of the two oldest in Milan and their Caucasian wingnut (mil_011) has no photograph; the garden publishes only a form, no address.
